value.body: A data analyst collects, cleans and studies data to answer business questions and builds reports and dashboards that teams use to make decisions. Employers include IT and analytics firms, banks, e-commerce, consulting and in-house business teams. A typical day involves writing SQL queries, preparing data in Excel or Python, and presenting findings.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any quantitative degree: B.Tech, B.Sc, BCA, BBA or B.Com

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, SQL, Power BI or Tableau, Python

items.label: Indian tech-sector workforce
items.note: Whole tech industry, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually get in as junior or associate analysts with demonstrated Excel, SQL and dashboard skills, often shown through small projects on public datasets. Internships and analytics roles in IT services firms are common entry points.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: A dashboard tool (Power BI or Tableau)

value.title: At a glance
items: Domain knowledge (finance, retail, health) increases value over time.
Next roles: senior analyst, analytics manager, data scientist.
Many applicants compete for entry roles, so a portfolio helps.

competition.note: BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
